knownDark: Finance and Growth tabs are placeholder cards.
There is no Tier 3 dev fixture; hero art exists only for Tier 1.
Every number is a first-pass placeholder — report felt wrongness ("nothing ever sells"), not suspected bad constants.
The balance harness bankrupts a competent bot before Tier 2. That is modeled and expected — don't be alarmed if a career gets tight.

sessions.label: Session A — a fresh Tier 1 career, 5 days

days.title: Day 0 — the managerial window
days.brief: Before you open the floor for the first time. You start with $50,000 cash, three seed cars (SUV, truck, sedan — recon-complete, priced at market retail, sellable today), an empty roster, Tier 1. All of that is intentional.

steps.text: Main Menu → New Game → name the slot → name your character, pick a backstory → Begin.
Sit on Home for a minute before doing anything at all.
Operations → Hiring → hire exactly ONE salesperson. Nothing else.
Look at the lot. Don't reprice anything — the seed asks are the baseline.
Tap Open Floor →.

probes.prompt: Sitting on Home before you touched anything — did you know what you were supposed to do next?

days.title: Day 1 — watch it
days.brief: Run this whole day at 1×, even though it's slow. You're calibrating your sense of the day's length and density before you start skipping. Watch how often a customer arrives, how often anything happens, whether the floor ever feels dead.

steps.text: Play the entire day at 1× — no speed control, no skip to close.
When it closes, read the Reveal all the way through before dismissing it.

probes.prompt: How long did the day FEEL at 1×?
Was there a stretch where nothing happened and you wanted to skip? When?
The Reveal at day-end — did you look forward to it, or dismiss it?

days.title: Day 2 — buy something
days.brief: Your first sourcing decision. Take the pre-purchase inspection on one car and skip it on the other — the contrast is the measurement.

steps.text: Operations → Visit Auction.
Buy one or two cars. Inspect one before buying; skip the inspection on the other.
Play the day at 2×.

probes.prompt: Did the auction feel like a real decision or a menu?
Did you have any basis for choosing WHAT to buy?
quick: Yes — I knew what I needed

days.title: Day 3 — the second hire
days.brief: This is the capacity measurement. One salesperson yesterday, two today — the question is whether the day visibly changes. If you can't tell the difference, say so plainly; that IS the finding.

steps.text: Before opening: hire a SECOND salesperson.
Play the day at 2×.

probes.prompt: Did the day visibly change with two salespeople — more customers worked, fewer walks, more gross?

days.title: Day 4 — move a price
days.brief: Two price moves in opposite directions on the same day. Note both numbers in the flag before you open, so the export has your starting point.

steps.text: Pick your oldest unsold unit and CUT its ask.
Pick another and RAISE its ask.
Tap ⚑ and note both numbers before you open.
Play the day at 2×.

probes.prompt: Did either price move do anything you could SEE?

days.title: Day 5 — read the room
days.brief: Play straight through, then read Home top-to-bottom. A readout you enjoy but never act on is a different verdict than one you skip.

steps.text: Play the day straight through.
Read Market — the demand readout (segment heat, observed mix, coverage gap).
Read the Market Report — the weekly column (only appears once a Monday boundary has passed).
Read the Industry Wire — the headline ticker, its Confirmed/Rumor/Recap badges, and the "What you're not reading" footer.

probes.prompt: Did any of the three change what you'd do tomorrow?
If a month close landed during the round: did you know how far you were from the next tier, and what to do about it?

days.title: Session B, Day 1 — the manager
days.brief: A different career: Main Menu → Start at Tier 2 (dev fixture). There is no Tier 3 fixture — T3 is unreachable under the current un-tuned gate thresholds. That's a known calibration item, not a bug to report.

steps.text: Main Menu → Start at Tier 2 (dev fixture).
People tab → Manager Status card.
Hire a used car manager if you don't have one.
Play the day.

probes.prompt: Is it clear what the manager is now doing FOR you — advising you, or acting on your behalf?

days.title: Session B, Day 2 — paid intel
days.brief: Known going in: the paid lanes are quiet unless you're actively trading. Block reports need your own transactions; competitor tracking needs rivals repricing. Judge it anyway.

steps.text: Industry Wire → subscribe to auction_data ($45/day) and/or competitor_tracking ($30/day).
Play the day.

days.title: Session B, Day 3 — service
days.brief: The second profit centre. The question is whether it reads as a business you run or a settings page you configure once.

steps.text: Hire a service advisor.
Operations → Service Overview.
Set a pricing posture.
Play the day.

probes.prompt: Does the service department read as a second business, or as a settings page?
